sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之爱及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在黑胶唱片时代在夜总会当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带300件你最珍贵的财产去上班，然后把DJ台变成这样一个活生生的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了美丽的50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Zolinkano-Youngs, filling in as hoSt. This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是代班主持佐林卡诺-杨斯。这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Tonight, relentless walls of flame raging across Europe.
sentences.zh: 今晚，无情的火墙在欧洲各地肆虐。

sentences.en: Firefighters say it's David versus Goliath.
sentences.zh: 消防员说这简直是大卫对战歌利亚。

sentences.en: A week after it started, they're still struggling.
sentences.zh: 火灾发生一周后，他们仍在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: To contain massive wildfires burning out of control in France and Spain.
sentences.zh: 以控制在法国和西班牙失控燃烧的大规模野火。

sentences.en: This summer, wildfires have been raging across Europe, with France and Spain particularly hard hit.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，野火在欧洲各地肆虐，法国和西班牙受灾尤其严重。

sentences.en: More than 360,000 residents in Taurus have now been evacuated.
sentences.zh: 陶尔斯现在已有36万多名居民被疏散。

sentences.en: It feels like we're in a war zone.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像身处战区。

sentences.en: The words of one woman living near Bordeaux as flames get ever closer.
sentences.zh: 一名住在波尔多附近的女性在烈火逼近时这样说道。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands of acres incinerated, villages destroyed, and entire communities upended by the fires.
sentences.zh: 数万英亩的土地被烧为灰烬，村庄被毁，整个社区被大火颠覆。

sentences.en: Police come and started screaming in the neighborhood like, you have to get out, get out.
sentences.zh: 警察来到社区开始大喊大叫，比如，你们必须离开，离开。

sentences.en: You have 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 你们只有20分钟。

sentences.en: Execuate.
sentences.zh: 执行。

sentences.en: Today, I talked to my colleagues Chico Harlan and Mark Landler about why this fire season has been especially devastating for Europe.
sentences.zh: 今天，我与我的同事奇科·哈兰和马克·兰德尔谈论了为什么这个火灾季节对欧洲来说格外具有毁灭性。

sentences.en: And how, when it comes to climate change, the continent is grappling with just how much it may need to adapt.
sentences.zh: 以及在气候变化方面，欧洲大陆正在艰难应对它可能需要进行多大程度的适应。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, July 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月30日，星期四。

sentences.en: Chico, welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 奇科，欢迎来到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 不用谢。

sentences.en: This is your first time on the show.
sentences.zh: 这是你第一次上这个节目。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I am glad to have you here.
sentences.zh: 好的，很高兴你能来这里。

sentences.en: You're the global climate correspondent at The New York Times, and you're based in Europe.
sentences.zh: 你是《纽约时报》的全球气候记者，常驻欧洲。

sentences.en: So, help us make sense of these fires that are sweeping across France and Spain.
sentences.zh: 那么，请帮我们理清席卷法国和西班牙的这些火灾。

sentences.en: What's your understanding of how both these countries get fires this big and destructive at the same time?
sentences.zh: 据你了解，这两个国家是如何同时发生如此巨大且具有破坏性的火灾的？

sentences.en: Well, you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你说得对。

sentences.en: These fires are simultaneously unfolding as the largest ever in France and the largest in Spain.
sentences.zh: 这些火灾同时爆发，是法国有史以来最大的一次，也是西班牙最大的一次。

sentences.en: They're both unfolding on the outskirts of major cities, Madrid and Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 它们都在马德里和波尔多等大城市的郊区爆发。

sentences.en: And there have been large-scale evacuations.
sentences.zh: 并且已经发生了大规模疏散。

sentences.en: And in order to really understand how you get two fires that are both historic, kind of have to go back all the way to May, when it wasn't even summer yet.
sentences.zh: 为了真正理解这两场历史性的火灾是如何发生的，我们不得不一直追溯到5月，当时甚至还不是夏天。

sentences.en: Europe is bracing for its first major heat event of 2026.
sentences.zh: 欧洲正严阵以待2026年的第一场重大高温事件。

sentences.en: That was the first time that Western Europe was hit by a heat wave.
sentences.zh: 那是西欧第一次遭到热浪袭击。

sentences.en: And it is punishingly hot.
sentences.zh: 而且热得折磨人。

sentences.en: People are scurrying for shade.
sentences.zh: 人们争相寻找阴凉处。

sentences.en: I'm taking a shower right before bed.
sentences.zh: 我在睡觉前冲个澡。

sentences.en: I'm sleeping with wet towels over me just to try to survive, honestly, and just try to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我盖着湿毛巾睡觉，老实说，只是为了努力活下来，努力睡个觉。

sentences.en: And then came the big one just a month later in late June.
sentences.zh: 仅仅一个月后的6月下旬，大热浪就来了。

sentences.en: The Eiffel Tower closed early due to safety concerns.
sentences.zh: 埃菲尔铁塔因安全问题提前关闭。

sentences.en: Temperatures in parts of France hitting 111 degrees.
sentences.zh: 法国部分地区的温度达到了111华氏度。

sentences.en: And if you just look at France for a second, in the span of three days, they set the hottest day in national history back to back to back.
sentences.zh: 如果你只看法国，在短短三天内，他们接连不断地刷新了国家历史上的最高气温纪录。

sentences.en: These are unprecedented times, said the French president.
sentences.zh: 法国总统表示，这是前所未有的时代。

sentences.en: And if that had just been a three-day thing, that alone would have been remarkable.
sentences.zh: 如果那只是三天的事，光是这一点就已经非同寻常了。

sentences.en: But the unusually hot temperatures stayed.
sentences.zh: 但异常的高温天气持续了下来。

sentences.en: And then they let up for a few days, and then they came roaring back through July.
sentences.zh: 然后它们减弱了几几天，接着在7月份卷土重来。

sentences.en: This morning, the death toll keeps climbing due to the brutal heat wave gripping Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 今天早上，由于肆虐西欧的残酷热浪，死亡人数不断攀升。

sentences.en: It was very lethal.
sentences.zh: 这是非常致命的。

sentences.en: A public institute in Spain says there were more than a thousand excess heat-related deaths this June.
sentences.zh: 西班牙的一个公共机构表示，今年6月与高温相关的超额死亡人数超过了一千人。

sentences.en: Some estimates say 10,000 extra deaths because of heat.
sentences.zh: 一些估计说，由于高温导致了1万例额外死亡。

sentences.en: Some have said 20,000.
sentences.zh: 有人说2万。

sentences.en: But what you can say for sure is that this was a highly deadly event across Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 但你可以确定的是，这是西欧发生的一场高度致命的事件。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay, so you're saying tens of thousands of people are dying in these heat waves.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也就是说有数万人死于这些热浪中。

sentences.en: In the U.S., we often see a couple thousand people die annually, and that's awful.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我们经常看到每年有几千人死亡，这太可怕了。

sentences.en: But what you're describing is striking here.
sentences.zh: 但你在这里描述的情况令人震惊。

sentences.en: Why is this toll so big?
sentences.zh: 为什么死亡人数这么多？

sentences.en: There's a couple reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这有几个原因。

sentences.en: One is Europe has buildings that are older and that were not built for this climate.
sentences.zh: 一个是欧洲的建筑物更老旧，不是为这种气候建造的。

sentences.en: They're built for colder temperatures, and they were built to retain heat.
sentences.zh: 它们是为更寒冷的温度建造的，并且是为了保温而建造的。

sentences.en: In Paris, these famous beautiful homes, apartments, are under zinc roofs, which basically are like ovens.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎，这些著名的美丽房屋和公寓都有锌制屋顶，基本上就像烤箱一样。

sentences.en: Then, of course, there's the air conditioning factor, which is a big one.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有空调因素，这是一个大问题。

sentences.en: Still, a minority of Europeans have air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 至今，只有少数欧洲人拥有空调。

sentences.en: And then, during heat waves, people who can will scramble for anything during a daytime.
sentences.zh: 然后，在热浪期间，有条件的人会在白天争相寻找任何东西。

sentences.en: They'll go to a mall.
sentences.zh: 他们会去商场。

sentences.en: They'll jump in a pool.
sentences.zh: 他们会跳进游泳池。

sentences.en: But people who are elderly or have pre-existing conditions can be stuck in apartments that just never cool down and stay hot in the night.
sentences.zh: 但老年人或有基础疾病的人可能会被困在永远无法冷却、在夜间保持炎热的公寓里。

sentences.en: And after days, their bodies break down.
sentences.zh: 几天后，他们的身体就会崩溃。

sentences.en: And that's how these deaths happen.
sentences.zh: 这就是这些死亡发生的方式。

sentences.en: God, so people are literally baking right now, and it's because of a lack of air conditioning and the architecture of buildings.
sentences.zh: 天哪，所以人们现在真的在被烘烤，这是因为缺乏空调和建筑结构。

sentences.en: I'm going to ask, and I understand this, the most American question, but I do think it's a question that's on the minds of many listeners.
sentences.zh: 我要问一个，而且我理解这会是一个非常美国式的问题，但我确实认为这也是许多听众心中的疑问。

sentences.en: Why not use more air conditioning?
sentences.zh: 为什么不多用点空调？

sentences.en: I get there are environmental concerns, but explain this to me.
sentences.zh: 我知道有环保方面的顾虑，但请向我解释一下。

sentences.en: This situation seems dire.
sentences.zh: 这种情况似乎很严峻。

sentences.en: Well, it just requires money and time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这只是需要金钱和时间。

sentences.en: And in some cases, the design of the buildings presents a problem for installing air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，建筑的设计给安装空调带来了问题。

sentences.en: There's also, widespread in France, especially, a philosophical opposition to air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 此外，尤其在法国，普遍存在对空调的哲学反对态度。

sentences.en: But you have to remember that the idea was, look, this intense discomfort is a couple nights a year.
sentences.zh: 但你必须记住，当时的理念是，看，这种强烈的闷热一年也就几个晚上。

sentences.en: Like, we can deal with it when it gets bad.
sentences.zh: 就像，当情况变得糟糕时我们可以应付。

sentences.en: The rest of the year, there's no need for air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 一年中的其余时间，根本不需要空调。

sentences.en: What's happened this summer is that these periods of discomfort, and now deadly discomfort, are lasting for weeks, not just a couple days and go away.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天发生的事情是，这些让人不适、现在甚至是致命不适的时期持续了几个星期，而不仅仅是几天就过去。

sentences.en: Okay, so I just want to zoom out.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只是想退一步看宏观。

sentences.en: Why is it so much hotter?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这么热？

sentences.en: Obviously, climate change, I assume, is a big part of this answer.
sentences.zh: 显然，我猜气候变化是这个答案的很大一部分。

sentences.en: But just explain what is making this heat wave so acute in these particular areas.
sentences.zh: 但请解释一下，是什么让这场热浪在这些特定地区如此剧烈。

sentences.en: Climate change is the global answer, but there is a more Europe-specific answer, too, which is how climate change is playing out there.
sentences.zh: 气候变化是全球性的答案，但也有一个更具欧洲特色的答案，那就是气候变化在那里是如何上演的。

sentences.en: A big part of the reason that Europe is warming faster is because of proximity to the Arctic.
sentences.zh: 欧洲变暖速度更快的一个重要原因是它靠近北极。

sentences.en: The Arctic is the fastest warming part of the whole planet.
sentences.zh: 北极是整个星球变暖最快的地区。

sentences.en: And why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: It's because this place that had snow cover and ice basically was like a white reflecting sheet.
sentences.zh: 这是因为这个曾经有积雪覆盖和冰层的地方基本上就像一张白色的反光板。

sentences.en: And that whiteness is now being lost and gradually turning into more darker surfaces, dark waters, places where there's no longer ice or snow.
sentences.zh: 这种白色现在正在逐渐消失，并逐渐变成更多的深色表面、深色水域，那些不再有冰雪的地方。

sentences.en: And now, whereas the sun used to bounce back up, now that radiation and heat is being absorbed into the waters.
sentences.zh: 现在，以前阳光会反射回去，而现在辐射和热量正被吸收到水体中。

sentences.en: You can think of it like a t-shirt on a hot day.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它想象成热天里的T恤。

sentences.en: We wear a white t-shirt, it bounces back the heat.
sentences.zh: 我们穿白色T恤，它能反射热量。

sentences.en: You wear a black t-shirt.
sentences.zh: 你穿黑色T恤。

sentences.en: You're extremely hot.
sentences.zh: 你会非常热。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And right now, the Arctic is that black t-shirt.
sentences.zh: 而现在，北极就是那件黑色T恤。

sentences.en: And that is causing these ripple effects.
sentences.zh: 这正在引发连锁反应。

sentences.en: What it adds up to is that Europe has been warming by about 0.5 Celsius, which is almost a degree Fahrenheit, per decade.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，欧洲每十年气温上升约0.5摄氏度，几乎是华氏一度。

sentences.en: That doesn't sound like a big number, but you spread that out and aggregate it over a couple decades.
sentences.zh: 这听起来不是一个大数字，但如果你把它摊开并在几十年内累计起来。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, you have a climate that feels different than even what you remember 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，你会发现气候的感觉甚至与你20年前记忆中的不同了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So let's talk about these fires.
sentences.zh: 那我们来谈谈这些火灾。

sentences.en: We've got this intense heat.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了这种酷热。

sentences.en: Is it as simple as that?
sentences.zh: 事情就这么简单吗？

sentences.en: It's a lot hotter, so things will burn more easily?
sentences.zh: 天气热得多，所以东西更容易燃烧？

sentences.en: It is pretty straightforward, and that's especially true when heat lasts for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这其实挺简单的，当热浪持续很长时间时尤其如此。

sentences.en: There's a big difference between a one-day spike and a spike that goes on for weeks.
sentences.zh: 单日的高温峰值和持续数周的峰值有很大区别。

sentences.en: And there are other factors at play, too, that are a little bit more in the background.
sentences.zh: 还有其他一些更处于背景中的因素也在发挥作用。

sentences.en: I mean, one is just depopulation of rural areas, more intensification of agriculture, but smaller plots of farmland that are being used.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个是农村地区人口减少，农业集约化程度提高，但使用的农田地块变小了。

sentences.en: And so more of Europe is being overtaken by foreSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，越来越多的欧洲土地被森林占领。

sentences.en: And that is definitely what happened in this part of southwestern France.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是法国西南部这一地区发生的事情。

sentences.en: That area that's burning used to be swampland.
sentences.zh: 正在燃烧的那个地区曾经是沼泽地。

sentences.en: And in the 19th century, the government planted pine forests there.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪，政府在那里种植了松树林。

sentences.en: And these monoculture forests, as they're called, often burn more easily than ones that are mixed.
sentences.zh: 这些所谓的单一文化森林，通常比混合林更容易燃烧。

sentences.en: This is the kind of decision that's not so consequential when France has the climate that it had historically.
sentences.zh: 当法国拥有其历史上那样的气候时，这种决定并不是那么重要。

sentences.en: But you combine that with what's changing because of climate change, and all of a sudden having pine forests becomes a huge liability.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把它与气候变化带来的改变结合起来，突然之间拥有松树林就成了一个巨大的隐患。

sentences.en: Okay, so they planted a bunch of trees.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以他们种了一堆树。

sentences.en: And in the process, it seems like they inadvertently created a tinderbox.
sentences.zh: 在这个过程中，他们似乎无意中制造了一个火药桶。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think the conclusion that you get from that and from so much else that you're seeing here is that Europe simply had built itself up in the natural world and in the physical world for an environment that no longer exists.
sentences.zh: 我认为你从中以及在这里看到的其他很多事情中得出的结论是，欧洲根本就是在自然界和物理世界中为一种已经不复存在的环境构建了自己。

sentences.en: You just think about the cities alone and the consequences and problems that can come from thinking about how do we make the cities more livable during periods of intense heat.
sentences.zh: 你只要想想城市本身，以及思考如何在酷热时期让城市更宜居所带来的后果和问题。

sentences.en: And indeed, Paris has been a pretty good example of a place that has gone all in on trying to better equip itself by cutting the number of vehicles in the city,
sentences.zh: 事实上，巴黎一直是一个很好的例子，它全力以赴通过减少城里的汽车数量来更好地武装自己，

sentences.en: by expanding green space.
sentences.zh: 通过扩大绿地空间。

sentences.en: All these things have essentially made Paris the best in class example in Europe.
sentences.zh: 所有这些基本上都使巴黎成为欧洲同类中的最佳典范。

sentences.en: And yet, these heat waves are still extremely deadly.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些热浪仍然极其致命。

sentences.en: So this is where you start to see these compounding challenges add up.
sentences.zh: 这就是你开始看到这些复合挑战累积起来的地方。

sentences.en: And the bigger point is that this is a global problem, and Europe is at the mercy of the bigger emitting countries, China, India, the United States,
sentences.zh: 更重要的一点是，这是一个全球性问题，欧洲受制于排放大国——中国、印度、美国，

sentences.en: not to mention fast-growing developing countries where there's huge energy demands, and those demands will continue to be growing.
sentences.zh: 更不用说那些能源需求巨大的快速发展的国家，这些需求将继续增长。

sentences.en: So these are the places that are going to be determining the trajectory for the world with their decisions, how much solar, how much coal.
sentences.zh: 因此，正是这些地方将通过他们的决定——多少太阳能、多少煤炭——来决定世界的轨迹。

sentences.en: These are really complicated questions, and at stake is how quickly we change the industries and societies we've built up based on fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 这些都是非常复杂的问题，危及的是我们以化石燃料为基础建立起来的产业和社会的改变速度。

sentences.en: So that's not a question where Europe has primacy to make a determination, and it is the definition of a global issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是一个欧洲拥有首要决定权的问题，这正是全球性问题的定义。

sentences.en: Well, Chico, thanks for explaining how we got here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，奇科，谢谢你解释我们是如何走到这一步的。

sentences.en: Appreciate you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Happy to do it.
sentences.zh: 乐意效劳。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: After the break, I talked to my colleague Mark Landler, who is on the ground in France, about how the country is reckoning with the toll of these disasters.
sentences.zh: 休息过后，我与身在法国现场的同事马克·兰德尔谈了谈该国是如何应对这些灾难带来的损失的。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星之外是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 Super Sundays.
sentences.zh: 60个超级星期天。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
sentences.zh: 两万五千个食谱。

sentences.en: And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢一锅出食谱，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您理解世界，充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，即可在 nytimes.com slash subscribe 享受优惠。

sentences.en: Mark, my friend, I'm glad you're here.
sentences.zh: 马克，我的朋友，很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: Great to be with you, Zolan.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起，佐兰。

sentences.en: We just talked to Chico Harlan about how we got to the point of this record heat wave and subsequently these devastating wildfires.
sentences.zh: 我们刚和奇科·哈兰谈过，探讨了我们是如何走到创纪录热浪这一步，以及随之而来的毁灭性野火。

sentences.en: But you, sir, are bearing witness.
sentences.zh: 但你，先生，正在亲历这一切。

sentences.en: And I want you to tell me what you have seen.
sentences.zh: 我想让你告诉我你都看到了什么。

sentences.en: What does it look like from the ground in a place like Bordeaux?
sentences.zh: 在波尔多这样地方的地面上，情况是怎样的？

sentences.en: So, I arrived in Bordeaux last Sunday at around 3.30, 4 o'clock in the afternoon.
sentences.zh: 所以，我上周日下午三点半左右、四点左右抵达了波尔多。

sentences.en: And that was a particularly bad day because the wind was blowing from the west to the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 那是个格外糟糕的日子，因为风是从西向东吹的。

sentences.en: So, all the smoke from the fire was blowing directly over the city from a distance of about 20 miles away.
sentences.zh: 因此，大火产生的所有烟雾直接从大约20英里外吹过整座城市。

sentences.en: So, as the train pulled into this very beautiful old soaring station, there was a really apocalyptic scene.
sentences.zh: 所以，当火车驶入这座非常美丽古老、高耸的车站时，眼前的景象简直像世界末日。

sentences.en: A sort of a deep yellow-orange cloud that was sort of hanging over the entire city.
sentences.zh: 一种深黄橙色的云雾笼罩在整座城市上空。

sentences.en: You couldn't see the sun.
sentences.zh: 你根本看不到太阳。

sentences.en: It really had blotted out the sun.
sentences.zh: 它真的把太阳给遮蔽了。

sentences.en: The spires of the cathedral, which are a real landmark in Bordeaux, So, you could sort of barely pick them out in the distance.
sentences.zh: 大教堂的尖顶是波尔多的一个标志性景观，所以你勉强能在远处辨认出它们的轮廓。

sentences.en: And then when the train pulled in and we all stepped off and walked down the platform, you instantly smelled this kind of deep, smoky smell in the air.
sentences.zh: 然后，当火车进站，我们都下车走上站台时，你立刻闻到空气中弥漫着这种浓烈、烟熏的气味。

sentences.en: And then as you walked out of the station and into the street, you actually began to see before your eyes these tiny pieces of ash floating in the air.
sentences.zh: 接着，当你走 出车站来到街上，你实际上开始亲眼看到空气中漂浮着这些微小的灰烬颗粒。

sentences.en: And you instantly felt it in your throat.
sentences.zh: 你立刻在喉咙里感受到了。

sentences.en: You felt it on your eyes.
sentences.zh: 你的眼睛也能感觉到。

sentences.en: It was like walking into a sort of a very dystopian kind of landscape.
sentences.zh: 这就像是走进了某种极其反乌托邦的风景之中。

sentences.en: And it sort of very instantly brought home that this is an atmosphere in a city that was in a lot of distress.
sentences.zh: 这立刻让人深切意识到，这座城市正处于极度困境之中。

sentences.en: Okay, you're at the train station.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你到了火车站。

sentences.en: You're going towards Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 你正前往波尔多。

sentences.en: But I'm imagining most of the people that you're seeing, they're trying to get out of Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 但我想象你看到的大多数人，他们正试图离开波尔多。

sentences.en: They're trying to flee the area, right?
sentences.zh: 他们正试图逃离这个地区，对吧？

sentences.en: There were a lot of people in the station making plans to leave the city.
sentences.zh: 车站里有很多人在计划离开这座城市。

sentences.en: My goal was to get as quickly as I could to one of these huge evacuation centers that had been set up around the city to accommodate people who'd been forced to flee their houses.
sentences.zh: 我的目标是尽快赶到围绕城市设立的大型疏散中心之一，那里用于安置被迫逃离家园的人们。

sentences.en: So, that was my first sort of destination as I began reporting the story.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我开始报道这个故事时的第一个目的地。

sentences.en: Okay, so you're at the evacuation center.
sentences.zh: 好的，那你现在在疏散中心了。

sentences.en: Tell me about the stories you heard while you were there.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲你在那里的所见所闻吧。

sentences.en: First of all, just to set the scene, you walk into this enormous airplane hangar-sized room where there are hundreds and hundreds of cots in rows.
sentences.zh: 首先，为了交代背景，你走进这个巨大的、飞机机库大小的房间里，里面排满了成百上千张行军床。

sentences.en: And people either lying on the cots, sitting on the cots.
sentences.zh: 人们要么躺在床上，要么坐在床上。

sentences.en: Some of them are playing cards.
sentences.zh: 他们有的人在打牌。

sentences.en: A lot of them are sitting in groups.
sentences.zh: 很多人三五成群地坐在一起。

sentences.en: So, I sort of walked around.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在周围转了转。

sentences.en: I brought a news assistant from our bureau and the two of us began talking to people.
sentences.zh: 我从我们分社带了一位新闻助理，我们俩开始和人们交谈。

sentences.en: The first two people that we encountered were a younger woman and an older woman, both of whom had fled their apartments in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到的前两个人是一个年轻女性和一个年长女性，两人都是在半夜逃离了公寓。

sentences.en: They'd been rousted almost literally out of bed by the police, knocking on their doors, telling them they had to leave now.
sentences.zh: 她们几乎可以说是被警察从床上拉起来的，警察敲门告诉她们必须马上离开。

sentences.en: They knew the previous evening that things were getting dire.
sentences.zh: 前一天晚上她们就知道情况越来越危急了。

sentences.en: One of them told me that she stood on the balcony of her fifth-floor apartment and sort of could see the wall of flames only a mile or so from her apartment.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人告诉我，她站在五楼公寓的阳台上，能看到离她公寓只有大约一英里远的火墙。

sentences.en: And so, these women were really truly worried about what they would find when they got a chance to go home, whether their apartments would still be intact.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些女性真的很担心她们有机会回家时会看到什么，她们的公寓是否还完好无损。

sentences.en: And so, these were the kinds of stories, and they were reflected really over and over and over again as you looked out across this cavernous room.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是这类故事，当你放眼望去这个巨大的房间时，它们真的在不断地重演。

sentences.en: There were a lot of people who were feeling really in a very exposed and dangerous position,
sentences.zh: 有很多人觉得自己处于一个非常暴露和危险的境地，

sentences.en: filled with fear about the future, about the state of their houses, the things they left behind, and how difficult it would be to pick up the pieces.
sentences.zh: 内心充满了对未来、对房屋状况、对留下的物品以及收拾残局会有多困难的恐惧。

sentences.en: This sounds devastating.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太毁灭性了。

sentences.en: I mean, the world is getting a glimpse of this devastation.
sentences.zh: 我是说，世界正在窥见这种毁灭的冰山一角。

sentences.en: We're seeing these scattered videos of people fleeing their homes.
sentences.zh: 我们看到这些零星的视频，记录了人们逃离家园的场景。

sentences.en: I've seen residents that are choosing to jump in and fight these fires and help firefighters, but you're really painting a full picture of this.
sentences.zh: 我看到有居民选择加入并扑灭这些大火、协助消防员，但你真的在全面描绘这幅画面。

sentences.en: And so far, specifically with France, what's been burned in the path of these fires?
sentences.zh: 那么到目前为止，特别是在法国，这些大火的路径上有什么被烧毁了？

sentences.en: What has been ultimately destroyed?
sentences.zh: 最终有什么被摧毁了？

sentences.en: Just to give you a couple sort of headline numbers, we're talking about over 100,000 acres of property.
sentences.zh: 为了给你提供一些概括性的数字，我们讨论的是超过10万英亩的土地。

sentences.en: Many, many, many villages have been damaged.
sentences.zh: 许许多多的村庄受到了破坏。

sentences.en: One village in particular, La Porge, which is west of Bordeaux, has suffered catastrophic damage with some 150 homes utterly destroyed.
sentences.zh: 其中一个村庄拉波尔日，位于波尔多以西，遭受了灾难性的破坏，大约有150所房屋被彻底摧毁。

sentences.en: And something in excess of 240,000 people were forced to evacuate their homes.
sentences.zh: 超过24万人被迫撤离家园。

sentences.en: That makes this the largest peacetime evacuation in modern French history.
sentences.zh: 这使得它成为现代法国历史上最大规模的和平时期疏散行动。

sentences.en: And so we're really, you know, talking about a magnitude of natural disaster that may be familiar to people in other countries,
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的，你知道的，在讨论一场也许其他国家的人们会觉得熟悉的自然灾害的规模，

sentences.en: but in France, it is really, truly something that no one has ever seen.
sentences.zh: 但在法国，这确实是前所未有的。

sentences.en: So given that this is much bigger than past fires, do they have resources?
sentences.zh: 既然这比过去的火灾要大得多，他们有资源吗？

sentences.en: Do they know how to fight this thing?
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何对抗这个东西吗？

sentences.en: Are they fully equipped in this moment?
sentences.zh: 他们目前装备齐全吗？

sentences.en: Well, France has invested a fair amount in firefighting capacity, in part drawing on the experience of some of the bad fire seasons that they've had in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，法国在消防能力上投入了相当多的资金，部分借鉴了过去经历的一些严重火灾季的经验。

sentences.en: So yes, they do.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，他们有。

sentences.en: They have Canadair planes that are capable of spraying fire retardant on the foreSt.
sentences.zh: 他们有能够向森林喷洒阻燃剂的加拿大飞机。

sentences.en: They've also had some very large planes loaned to them by some of their European neighbors.
sentences.zh: 一些欧洲邻国还借给他们一些非常大型的飞机。

sentences.en: So there are a great deal of resources in the region.
sentences.zh: 因此该地区有大量的资源。

sentences.en: But it has to be said, despite all that power they're bringing to this, the fires continue to burn out of control.
sentences.zh: 但必须指出的是，尽管他们投入了所有这些力量，大火仍在失控地燃烧。

sentences.en: So it's a pitched battle.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场激烈的战斗。

sentences.en: They're bringing a lot to it.
sentences.zh: 他们投入了大量的人力物力。

sentences.en: But it is, you know, far from under control yet.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，距离得到控制还差得远呢。

sentences.en: And we often see that there's real challenges when it comes to these responses to wildfires about where to prioritize your resources, right?
sentences.zh: 我们经常看到，在应对这些野火时，真正的挑战在于如何确定资源优先级的排序，对吧？

sentences.en: Have there been some of those points of tension when it comes to this response?
sentences.zh: 在应对过程中出现过这种紧张点吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, there have.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，有过。

sentences.en: And the reasons for that are that the region around Bordeaux has a lot of different sort of elements to it.
sentences.zh: 原因在于波尔多周边的地区有许多不同的要素。

sentences.en: There is a peninsula out by the ocean that's called the La Frère Peninsula.
sentences.zh: 靠近海洋有一个半岛，叫做拉弗雷尔半岛。

sentences.en: That is very popular with holiday makers.
sentences.zh: 那里非常受度假者的欢迎。

sentences.en: And people have vacation homes out there.
sentences.zh: 人们在那里有度假屋。

sentences.en: There are already some complaints from residents of this little town I mentioned, La Porge, which was so heavily damaged
sentences.zh: 我提到的那个受损严重的小镇拉波尔日的居民已经开始有一些抱怨，

sentences.en: that they were sort of essentially left to fend for themselves and that other areas, perhaps more economically advantaged areas, had more protection.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上被抛弃，只能自生自灭，而其他可能经济条件更好的地区得到了更多的保护。

sentences.en: We haven't confirmed those reports yet, but those are the types of things that you're beginning to hear about.
sentences.zh: 我们尚未证实这些报道，但这些是你开始听到的一些情况。

sentences.en: Then much closer to town, you have a series of very sensitive military installations where French companies manufacture components
sentences.zh: 离城镇更近的地方，有一系列高度敏感的军事设施，法国公司在那里制造组件

sentences.en: and propellant for the nuclear missile arsenal of France.
sentences.zh: 以及法国核导弹武库的推进剂。

sentences.en: Wait, time out.
sentences.zh: 等等，暂停一下。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: But we're talking about, when I think of Bordeaux, I definitely think of the wine industry.
sentences.zh: 但我们正在谈论的是，当我想起波尔多时，我绝对会想到葡萄酒产业。

sentences.en: I think of tourism.
sentences.zh: 我想到了旅游业。

sentences.en: You're saying that there's actually a nuclear facility in this area as well that could be in the line of these wildfires?
sentences.zh: 你是说这个地区实际上还有一个核设施，也可能处于这些野火的威胁路径上？

sentences.en: That seems terrifying.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太可怕了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm going to get to the vineyards.
sentences.zh: 对，我会讲到葡萄园的。

sentences.en: Don't worry about that.
sentences.zh: 不用担心那个。

sentences.en: But yeah, there are, in fact, factories that make rocket fuel.
sentences.zh: 但确实，事实上有一些制造火箭燃料的工厂。

sentences.en: Not far from Bordeaux and which lie in the path of these fires.
sentences.zh: 距离波尔多不远，并且位于这些野火的路径上。

sentences.en: So you can imagine that for the authorities, the top priority is preventing the fires from getting close enough to these factories that it would raise a question
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，对当局来说，首要任务是防止大火靠这些工厂太近，以免引发问题

sentences.en: about causing explosions.
sentences.zh: 导致爆炸。

sentences.en: Because that would, of course, take this into a very, very different magnitude in terms of a civil emergency.
sentences.zh: 因为那当然会将这起事件推向完全不同量级的民事紧急情况。

sentences.en: Yeah, I would say so.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想是的。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's obviously a concern on its own.
sentences.zh: 好的，这显然是一个独立的问题。

sentences.en: But let's go back to what you mentioned before.
sentences.zh: 但让我们回到你之前提到的内容。

sentences.en: Let's get back to the wine.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到葡萄酒上。

sentences.en: We know this is something that's incredibly important to the local economy in this region.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这对该地区的当地经济极其重要。

sentences.en: So tell me how the fires are impacting the wine industry, the vineyards in this area.
sentences.zh: 所以请告诉我大火是如何影响葡萄酒产业、这个地区的葡萄园的。

sentences.en: It's an interesting question, and the answer might surprise you a little.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的问题，答案可能会让你有点意外。

sentences.en: None of the vineyards so far have been directly affected by fire.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，没有任何葡萄园直接受到火灾的影响。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: And there are a number of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后有几个原因。

sentences.en: Part of it is geographic.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是地理原因。

sentences.en: A lot of the wine industry in Bordeaux is actually on the east side of the river, and the wildfires are on the west side of the river,
sentences.zh: 波尔多的许多葡萄酒产业实际上在河的东侧，而野火在河的西侧，

sentences.en: and indeed on the west side of the city of Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 而且确实在波尔多市的西侧。

sentences.en: Okay, so it's got a buffer right now.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以它现在有一个缓冲区。

sentences.en: There is a buffer.
sentences.zh: 确实有一个缓冲区。

sentences.en: There is also a separate issue, which is that vineyards can often act as a fire break, because the nature of vineyards are there's very little brush.
sentences.zh: 还有一个单独的问题，那就是葡萄园通常可以充当防火隔离带，因为葡萄园的特点是灌木丛非常少。

sentences.en: They're very well tended.
sentences.zh: 它们得到了很好的照料。

sentences.en: The soil around them tends to be fairly dry, and as a result, they aren't a particularly great accelerant for fires.
sentences.zh: 它们周围的土壤往往相当干燥，因此，它们并不是特别好的火灾助燃剂。

sentences.en: So the long and short of it is, no vineyard has erupted in flames during the course of these wildfires.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，在这些野火蔓延期间，没有任何葡萄园燃起大火。

sentences.en: But that isn't the end of the problem for the wine industry, because what has happened is that the vineyards, like the city itself,
sentences.zh: 但这并不是葡萄酒产业麻烦的结束，因为发生的情况是，葡萄园和这座城市本身一样，

sentences.en: have been covered with this very dark, smoky cloud.
sentences.zh: 都被这种非常黑暗、烟雾弥漫的云层所覆盖。

sentences.en: And the big question, and it's an unresolved one so far, is whether the smoke will hang over the vines long enough to permeate into the grapes themselves.
sentences.zh: 最大的问题（目前尚未解决）是烟雾是否会在葡萄藤上停留足够长的时间，以至于渗透到葡萄本身中。

sentences.en: And if it does do that, will it leave this vintage, when these grapes are harvested, will it leave this vintage with a kind of a smoky taste that could actually ruin the vintage
sentences.zh: 如果确实如此，这会不会让这一年份的酒在这些葡萄收获时带有一种烟熏味，从而毁了这一年份

sentences.en: were it strong enough?
sentences.zh: 如果烟味足够强烈的话？

sentences.en: I just want to clarify, if what you're describing actually happens, this isn't just like a blow to wine lovers.
sentences.zh: 我只想澄清一下，如果你所描述的情况真的发生了，这不仅仅是对葡萄酒爱好者的打击。

sentences.en: Like, this would be a major economic blow to the region, no?
sentences.zh: 比如，这对该地区将是一个重大的经济打击，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, it would.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, wine is one of the most important industries for Bordeaux.
sentences.zh: 我是说，葡萄酒是波尔多最重要的产业之一。

sentences.en: It's also the industry that has put Bordeaux on the map.
sentences.zh: 它也是让波尔多闻名世界的产业。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And even before these fires, the wine growers were facing a confluence of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 甚至在这些火灾之前，葡萄种植者就面临着一系列问题的交织。

sentences.en: President Trump's tariffs on French wine, an issue that you know well, Zolan.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统对法国葡萄酒加征关税，这是你很清楚的问题，佐兰。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And not just the fires, but successive summers of extreme heat, which have changed the harvest cycle.
sentences.zh: 不仅是火灾，还有连续几个夏天的极端高温，这改变了收获周期。

sentences.en: They've also changed the nature of the grapes in a way that makes it harder to produce the kind of finely balanced wine that Bordeaux is so famous for.
sentences.zh: 它们还改变了葡萄的性质，使得人们更难酿造出波尔多闻名遐迩的那种微妙平衡的葡萄酒。

sentences.en: So I think the people who live there recognize that the natural habitat that they live in is no longer well-suited to the kind of climate that they now face.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那里的人们认识到，他们赖以生存的自然栖息地已不再适合他们现在面临的气候。

sentences.en: This is just a much more hostile and unforgiving climate and one for which they're not particularly well-suited and one that will make it harder for them to make a living
sentences.zh: 这只是一个更加恶劣和无情的环境，一个他们不太适应的环境，这将使他们更难维持生计

sentences.en: the way that they have for generations.
sentences.zh: 像他们几代人那样。

sentences.en: What you're describing is is a longer-term struggle.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的是一场更长期的斗争。

sentences.en: There might be those who are waking up and asking, what the heck is going on?
sentences.zh: 可能会有人醒来后问，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: How did we get here?
sentences.zh: 我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: But you're more so saying there's been a series of steps over years that brought us to this point.
sentences.zh: 但你更倾向于说，多年来的一系列步骤把我们带到了这个点。

sentences.en: And I know we're talking about Bordeaux right now, but I should note there's also fires in Spain, devastating fires.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们现在在谈论波尔多，但我应该指出，西班牙也有火灾，毁灭性的火灾。

sentences.en: We're seeing this heat wave impact the European region more broadly.
sentences.zh: 我们看到这场热浪对欧洲地区的影响更为广泛。

sentences.en: And then I guess the question is, is this a tipping point, not just for Bordeaux, but for the country or even Europe in general?
sentences.zh: 然后我想问题是，这是否是一个转折点，不仅对波尔多，而且对整个国家甚至欧洲？

sentences.en: Well, as I'm sure Chico said earlier,
sentences.zh: 好吧，正如我相信奇科早些时候所说，

sentences.en: Europe is in a particularly exposed position because it's warming faster than any other continent on the planet and because it is not suited historically
sentences.zh: 欧洲处于一个特别脆弱的地位，因为它变暖的速度比地球上任何其他大陆都要快，而且它从历史上来看并不适应

sentences.en: to these kinds of dry, hot climates.
sentences.zh: 这种干燥、炎热的气候。

sentences.en: I think that Europe is facing a moment where people are really saying to themselves, we can't keep living the way we have.
sentences.zh: 我认为欧洲正面临这样一个时刻：人们真的在对自己说，我们不能再像以前那样生活了。

sentences.en: It simply doesn't work in the world that we are now entering.
sentences.zh: 它在我们现在进入的世界里根本行不通。

sentences.en: And this comes at a time when at a European level, there's quite a lot of backsliding on the ambitious targets that Europe set for making its economies a net zero.
sentences.zh: 正值此时，在欧洲层面，对于使经济实现净零排放的雄心勃勃的目标，出现了相当多的开倒车现象。

sentences.en: That is taking out as much greenhouse gases as they are putting into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 也就是消除与它们向大气中排放一样多的温室气体。

sentences.en: Climate policy has become controversial, particularly on the political right in France and other countries.
sentences.zh: 气候政策已经引发了争议，特别是在法国和其他国家的政治右翼中。

sentences.en: And so even as the evidence grows ever more dramatic of the changes to climate and the impacts of those changes, the political will to really confront climate change head on
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管有越来越多的戏剧性证据表明气候变化以及这些变化带来的影响，但真正正面应对气候变化的政治意愿

sentences.en: is actually weakened somewhat.
sentences.zh: 实际上有所削弱。

sentences.en: And that's a real paradox.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正的悖论。

sentences.en: This is fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: I literally think of France as a leader in this area.
sentences.zh: 我简直把法国看作这方面的领头羊。

sentences.en: Paris Climate Accords, right?
sentences.zh: 《巴黎气候协定》，对吧？

sentences.en: Why are we seeing this shift when it comes to the public?
sentences.zh: 为什么公众的态度会出现这种转变？

sentences.en: Well, there are a number of factors.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因素有很多。

sentences.en: The most important of which is the economy.
sentences.zh: 其中最重要的是经济。

sentences.en: Economic growth has been sluggish in France and other European countries.
sentences.zh: 法国和其他欧洲国家的经济增长一直很低迷。

sentences.en: There's also a great deal of energy insecurity as a result of the war in Ukraine and more recently, the closing of the Strait of Hormuz.
sentences.zh: 由于乌克兰战争，以及最近霍尔木兹海峡的关闭，也带来了极大的能源不安全感。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And in that kind of anxious environment, having a very aggressive green policy, net zero targets, seems to many like a luxury that Europe can't afford right now.
sentences.zh: 在那种充满焦虑的环境下，采取非常激进的绿色政策、净零目标，在许多人看来就像是欧洲目前负担不起的奢侈品。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: On one hand, you're describing a situation where economic anxiety is trumping all.
sentences.zh: 一方面，你描述的情况是经济焦虑占了上风。

sentences.en: It's shaping the public's attitude towards some of these ambitious goals when it comes to the climate.
sentences.zh: 它正在塑造公众对气候方面一些雄心勃勃的目标的态度。

sentences.en: On the other hand, this region is burning right now.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，这个地区现在正处于酷热之中。

sentences.en: And this would be the exact right time to recommit to some of these policies and goals.
sentences.zh: 而这正是重新承诺其中一些政策和目标的绝佳时机。

sentences.en: Well, indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think that political leaders are in fact hoping to seize this moment to do that, to perhaps turn the debate around a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我认为政治领导人实际上正希望抓住这个时刻来做到这一点，或许可以稍微扭转一下辩论的方向。

sentences.en: You saw that in Spain with the Prime Minister, Pedro Sanchez, who has declared what he calls a climate emergency.
sentences.zh: 你在西班牙的首相佩德罗·桑切斯身上看到了这一点，他宣布了所谓的紧急气候状态。

sentences.en: You know, I think you'll hear more voices like that in the coming days and weeks.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想你在接下来的几天和几周里会听到更多这样的声音。

sentences.en: But while this great debate plays out, people need solutions now.
sentences.zh: 但在这场激烈的辩论展开的同时，人们现在就需要解决方案。

sentences.en: They can't wait for three, four years.
sentences.zh: 他们等不及三、四年。

sentences.en: They need to learn how to live with and cope with this heat in the short run.
sentences.zh: 他们需要学会在短期内适应和应对这种酷热。

sentences.en: So what you're hearing a lot about in Europe these days is adaptation.
sentences.zh: 所以你最近在欧洲听到最多的是适应。

sentences.en: How do you adapt cultures and countries and societies to hotter climates?
sentences.zh: 如何让文化、国家和社会适应更炎热的气候？

sentences.en: And so clearly one of the easiest remedies is air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 很显然，最简单的救济方法之一就是空调。

sentences.en: And that's not to say that there's no air conditioning in France.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说法国没有空调。

sentences.en: There's plenty of air conditioning, particularly in the southern part of the country.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多空调，尤其是在南部地区。

sentences.en: But as a general principle,
sentences.zh: 但作为一个普遍原则，

sentences.en: France has moved more slowly and more reluctantly toward the widespread use of air conditioning, particularly in homes.
sentences.zh: 法国在普及空调方面步伐较慢，也比较勉强，尤其是在家庭中。

sentences.en: And I think what's happening now, and you're seeing it play out politically, culturally, is also a kind of a reckoning, a recognition that perhaps the French
sentences.zh: 我认为现在正在发生的事情，你从政治和文化层面上都能看到，也是一种清醒的认识，即法国人可能

sentences.en: are going to have to get over this.
sentences.zh: 必须克服这一点。

sentences.en: They're going to have to simply accept that widespread home air conditioning is going to be a reality in this country, just as it is in large parts of Spain,
sentences.zh: 他们必须简单地接受，在家里普遍安装空调将成为这个国家的现实，就像在西班牙的大部分地区一样，

sentences.en: just as it is in Dubai, just as it is in the United States.
sentences.zh: 就像在迪拜一样，就像在美国一样。

sentences.en: And I think based on my own reporting that France will get there another couple of summers like this, and it may get there sooner than we might expect.
sentences.zh: 根据我自己的报道，我认为法国再经历几个这样的夏天就会实现这一目标，而且它的到来可能会比我们预期的还要早。

sentences.en: I think that for the moment at least,
sentences.zh: 我认为至少目前而言，

sentences.en: Europe is caught in a situation where it's going to be thinking much more short-term about how do you cope with the next month, two months, and then let's address that epic issue
sentences.zh: 欧洲陷入了一种境地：它将更多地从短期考虑如何应对接下来的一两个月，然后让我们来解决那个史诗般的问题，

sentences.en: of can we get back to some really ambitious net zero targets?
sentences.zh: 即我们能否回到一些真正宏伟的净零排放目标上来？

sentences.en: Well, Mark, I hope you stay safe and cool.
sentences.zh: 好吧，马克，希望你注意安全，保持凉爽。

sentences.en: Appreciate you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Zolan.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，佐兰。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.zh: 我编写《连线》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天都创作

sentences.zh: 《拼字蜂》和《字母箱》游戏。

sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的现象。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.zh: 我能得出的唯一结论是，他把我叫到这个委员会面前的唯一原因，就是让我说点什么，

sentences.en: anything that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, behind bars, unquote.
sentences.zh: 任何可以证实他一再公开承诺的话，即用他的话说，引用“锒铛入狱”，反引号结束。

sentences.en: Appearing before a Senate committee on Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 周三出现在参议院委员会前时，

sentences.en: Dr. Anthony Fauci, the face of the government's response to the COVID pandemic, accused the committee's
sentences.zh: 安东尼·福奇博士作为政府应对新冠大流行时期的公众面孔，指责该委员会的

sentences.en: Republican leader,
sentences.zh: 共和党领袖、

sentences.en: Senator Rand Paul of Kentucky, of being on a crusade against him and refused to answer any questions.
sentences.zh: 来自肯塔基州的参议员兰德·保罗对他进行讨伐，并拒绝回答任何问题。

sentences.en: Therefore, although it pains me to do so because of the respect I have for the legislative branch of government, under the advice of my attorneys,
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管由于我对政府立法机构的尊重，这样做让我感到痛苦，但在我的律师的建议下，

sentences.en: I will invoke my right under the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution to refrain from answering your questions.
sentences.zh: 我将援引宪法第五修正案赋予我的权利，拒绝回答你的问题。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: The decision to not testify marked the latest turn in a feud between
sentences.zh: 拒绝作证的决定标志着

sentences.en: Dr. Fauci and Senator Paul, who has accused Fauci of lying to Congress.
sentences.zh: 福奇博士与参议员保罗之间恩怨的最新发展，后者曾指责福奇向国会撒谎。

sentences.en: An allegation
sentences.zh: 这是一个指控，

sentences.en: Fauci denies.
sentences.zh: 福奇予以否认。

sentences.en: Over the weekend,
sentences.zh: 周末，

sentences.en: Senator Paul released to the public
sentences.zh: 参议员保罗向公众公开了

sentences.en: Fauci's diary entries, in which the doctor reflected on the origins of COVID and mused over his own fame.
sentences.zh: 福奇的日记条目，这位医生在日记中反思了新冠病毒的起源，并对自己的名气进行了沉思。

sentences.en: And during the hearing, an irate Senator Paul kicked Fauci's attorney out of the hearing room.
sentences.zh: 在听证会期间，愤怒的参议员保罗将福奇的律师赶出了听证会大厅。

sentences.en: Look, this is the way
sentences.zh: 听着，这就是

sentences.en: Anthony Fauci wants to be remembered.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·福奇想要被记住的方式。

sentences.en: For a lawyer not listening to the rules, that's the way you want to be remembered and that's what you're going to do.
sentences.zh: 对于一个不听规则的律师来说，这就是你想被记住的方式，这就是你要做的。

sentences.en: You are not recognized, sir.
sentences.zh: 先生，你没有发言权。

sentences.zh: 对伊朗发起了新一轮袭击，特朗普政府称此举是为了报复针对美军的袭击企图。

sentences.en: forces.
sentences.zh: 部队。
